CENSUS CORRECTION (orchestrator, measured on origin/main @ 059d54b725).

The census posted on this epic moments ago is STALE — it was measured against an older main, before
this session's splits merged. It lists signing.py at 800, __main__.py at 798 and reconcile.py 799 as
uncovered; the first two are no longer near the cap at all.

MEASURED NOW, every src/rebar file >= 720 LOC:
  799  _engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile.py        RP-03 (diamond-flavoured-esok) — excluded
  793  llm/plan_review/det_floor.py                 THIS EPIC — in flight
  793  llm/plan_review/__init__.py                  sullen-famished-incatern — excluded
  791  _config_sources.py                           *** UNCOVERED — see below ***
  790  llm/workflow/executor.py                     THIS EPIC — in flight
  790  llm/plan_review/sidecar.py                   childproof-prominent-racerunner — excluded
  789  llm/prompting/prompts.py                     THIS EPIC — in flight
  786  _commands/init.py                            THIS EPIC — filed, not yet dispatched
  782  _engine/rebar_reconciler/applier.py          RP-03 + others — excluded

LANDED THIS SESSION, all now well under the cap and off the list entirely:
  signing.py 800 -> 435 (+216 +276)          Gerrit 1924
  apply_inbound_records.py 799 -> 390 + 470  Gerrit 1929
  inbound_differ.py 800 -> 540 + 312         Gerrit 1930
  __main__.py 804 -> under (+133 sibling)    Gerrit 1916
  config.py 799 -> 658 + 196                 Gerrit 1932

ONE GENUINE GAP the stale census got right for the wrong reason: `_config_sources.py` (791) is now
UNCOVERED. It was excluded from this epic's original scope because in-flight work owned it — that
work (masonic-abeyant-stagbeetle) has since CLOSED, so nothing claims it today. It is the only
near-cap file with no owner and no child here.

The observation that 36 files sit in the >= 720 warning band is worth keeping as a separate signal:
this epic drains the acute cases, but the band itself is the standing condition, and whether 800 is
the right number or the module boundaries are wrong is a larger question than this epic answers.
